survey: A wooden pier seen from the water side at a three-quarter angle. It runs along the shoreline and off the left edge of the card, with the sand beach behind it. The deck is a row of planks resting on a front beam. Round posts stand in the water below, and the two rear posts poke up through the deck as short stubs, lined up with their parts below the deck. One post near the middle rises above the deck and has a short metal peg. A red-and-white lifebuoy hangs on that peg through its hole, in front of the post. On the right, a front corner post stands in the water at the end of the planks with a thick rope coiled three times around its top. A side beam runs from there to a taller post further back on the right. The rope's free end drops from the coil, lies along the deck to the left and meets the right side of the lifebuoy.

errors.where: Rope between the coiled corner post and the lifebuoy, at the right edge of the ring
errors.what: The rope's free end runs along the deck and just stops where it touches the lifebuoy. There is no knot, loop or tie to the ring's grab line, so the rope does not clearly attach to anything at that end. It reads as a loose end.

fix: The rope coiled around the right corner post runs along the deck and is clearly tied to the lifebuoy's grab line with a visible knot. Alternatively, the rope's end stays tucked into the coil on the post.
